summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to make the child tax credit fully refundable for residents of Puerto Rico by modifying how their income is considered and how the refundable portion of the credit is calculated, effective for tax years beginning after December 31, 2024.

scores.thoughts: This bill expands the refundable portion of the child tax credit to residents of Puerto Rico and modifies the calculation of the refundable credit. This would result in increased outlays from the federal government, thus increasing government spending.

The bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to expand eligibility for the refundable child tax credit and adjust its calculation for Puerto Rico residents. This effectively reduces the tax burden for eligible families through increased refunds, which is a form of tax relief.

By increasing government outlays through expanded tax credits without identifying offsetting revenue, this bill would contribute to the national debt. The impact is moderate as it focuses on a specific population and credit expansion.
